sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: The frequency table shown summarizes the daily score measurements collected at the botanical conservatory. What is the mean of the data set?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $13$. From the frequency table, the values are $10, 12, 14, 16$ with frequencies $2, 4, 4, 2$. Because the distribution is symmetric about $\frac{12 + 14}{2} = 13$, the arithmetic mean is $\frac{10(2) + 12(4) + 14(4) + 16(2)}{12} = 13$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the water treatment plant, the mean of four numbers is 18. Three of the numbers are 12, 16, and 22. What is the fourth number?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $22$. Total sum = $4 \times 18 = 72$. Sum of three = $12 + 16 + 22 = 50$. Fourth number = $72 - 50 = 22$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the regional airport shuttle, in a calculation for the coastal aquarium (case 28), if five quiz scores have a sum of 420, what is the mean score?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $84$. Applying One-Variable Statistics, Distributions & Margin of Error principles, Mean = $420 / 5 = 84$. Therefore, the verified correct option is 84.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the glassblowing studio, in a class of 25 students, the median test score is 84. If 12 students scored above 84, how many students scored at or below 84?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $13$. Total students = 25. If 12 scored above 84, then $25 - 12 = 13$ scored at or below 84.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the ceramic studio, a data set of 9 numbers has a median of 15. If the number 15 is added to the data set, what is the new median?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $15$. Adding a number equal to the current median leaves the median unchanged at 15.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: During a 5-day study at the botanical conservatory, the mean number of adult tickets recorded per day was $20$. For the first four days, the counts were $15, 18, 21,$ and $22$. What was the count on the fifth day?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $24$. For 5 values to have a mean of $20$, their sum must equal $5 \times 20 = 100$. The sum of the first four values is $76$, so the fifth value is $100 - 76 = 24$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A random sample of visitors to the municipal library found that $36\%$ prefer hardcover books, with an associated margin of error of $\pm 4\%$. If a total of $3000$ visitors attend next month, what is the difference between the maximum and minimum plausible number of visitors expected to prefer hardcover books?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $240$. The plausible interval for the percentage is from $32\%$ to $40\%$, a span of $8\%$. Multiplying $3000$ by $8\% = 0.08$ gives $1200 - 960 = 240$ visitors.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: At the community theater, Data Set A consists of the 5 measurements $34, 38, 42, 46, 50$, and Data Set B consists of the 5 measurements $24, 33, 42, 51, 60$. What is the positive difference between the range of Data Set B and the range of Data Set A?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $20$. The range of Data Set B is $60 - 24 = 36$, and the range of Data Set A is $50 - 34 = 16$. The positive difference is $36 - 16 = 20$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: During a 5-day study at the regional bakery, the mean number of standard passes recorded per day was $23$. For the first four days, the counts were $18, 21, 24,$ and $25$. What was the count on the fifth day?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $27$. For 5 values to have a mean of $23$, their sum must equal $5 \times 23 = 115$. The sum of the first four values is $88$, so the fifth value is $115 - 88 = 27$.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: A random sample of visitors to the coastal aquarium found that $39\%$ prefer oak saplings, with an associated margin of error of $\pm 4\%$. If a total of $6000$ visitors attend next month, what is the difference between the maximum and minimum plausible number of visitors expected to prefer oak saplings?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $480$. The plausible interval for the percentage is from $35\%$ to $43\%$, a span of $8\%$. Multiplying $6000$ by $8\% = 0.08$ gives $2580 - 2100 = 480$ visitors.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging Synthesis (38–45)

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the mountain observatory, a researcher wants to study the sleeping habits of all college students in a state. Which sample is most representative?
choices: 50 students selected at random from the university library at midnight
500 students selected at random from across all colleges and universities in the state
200 students who volunteer to fill out an online sleep survey
questions.answer: Random selection across the entire population of interest (all colleges in the state) provides the most representative sample.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the urban bike-share station, what happens to the standard deviation of a data set if 10 is added to every data point?
questions.answer: Adding a constant shifts the distribution along the number line without altering the spread between data points, so standard deviation is unchanged.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the publishing house, a study randomly assigns 100 headache patients to receive either a new medication or a placebo. What type of study is this?
questions.answer: Treatments are actively imposed and participants are randomly assigned, making it a randomized controlled experiment.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: In a model for the recycling center, in a calculation for the local farmers market (case 70), why is random assignment used in experiments?
choices: To ensure the sample represents the entire global population
To balance confounding variables across treatment groups so causality can be established
To eliminate the need for a control group
To reduce the sample size needed
questions.answer: Random assignment distributes confounding variables evenly between groups, allowing researchers to infer cause-and-effect relationships.

questions.target: Mean, Median, Range, Standard Deviation & Margin of Error
questions.q: At the wildlife sanctuary, Data Set A consists of the 5 measurements $52, 56, 60, 64, 68$, and Data Set B consists of the 5 measurements $46, 53, 60, 67, 74$. What is the positive difference between the range of Data Set B and the range of Data Set A?
questions.answer: The range of Data Set B is $74 - 46 = 28$, and the range of Data Set A is $68 - 52 = 16$. The positive difference is $28 - 16 = 12$.

questions.q: At the sports complex, Data Set A consists of the 5 measurements $55, 59, 63, 67, 71$, and Data Set B consists of the 5 measurements $43, 53, 63, 73, 83$. What is the positive difference between the range of Data Set B and the range of Data Set A?
